additional_info.subject: RE: ID0477339-DC/Si-D/BE- [Y2 / S6 313717534008] Unstable CP Resistance CRM:03289000501
additional_info.body:
Hello Harun,
The customer asked me to turn off the charger, because their load management system is not completed yet, the installer still needs to install their local network cable.
I believe I found the root cause with the measurements I performed yesterday. The EGOC CP line voltages drops due to the resistance of the CP line cable inside of the CCS2 cable/plug.
When the CCS2 cable is connected the voltage on the CCS2 cable and also on the EGOG are jumping between -5 and +7Volts. Caused by the resistance measured on the CP cable internal of the CCS cable.
When I removed the brown CP wire from XD16, the ECOG voltages stayed at 12V.
I also kept the brown wire disconnected before leaving the site, because the charger acts like an EV is connected on plug B when powered on.
Hope this answers your questions. Feel free to give a call if needed.
Bas Jeurissen, Field Service Engineer
Siemens e-Mobility Charging B.V.
BIC 1, 5657BX, Eindhoven, Netherlands
Mobile: +31682058090

@siemens.com
